en.headline: Housing institute calls for a statutory building upkeep fund
en.dek: The Hong Kong Institute of Housing says owners should pay into a separate maintenance account as more than 24,000 buildings turn 50 by 2043.
body: The Hong Kong Institute of Housing on Thursday called on the government to give legal status to a building maintenance fund, arguing that regular contributions would ease the shock of large repair bills as the city's housing stock ages.

Institute president Rosita Wong said owners would be required to set up the fund and pay into it on an ongoing basis, typically as a share of the monthly management fee. The money would sit in a separate, independently ordered building account and be used for maintenance and repair works, rather than being raised only when a major job became unavoidable.

Wong said she hoped the arrangement could be put on a statutory footing as early as possible. She cited an ageing crisis in which more than 24,000 buildings in Hong Kong are expected to be 50 years old or above by 2043. A mandatory fund, she said, would shift maintenance from a reactive model to a planned one, reduce the burden on individual owners and cut pressure on public finance.
She also welcomed a pre-approved list of contractors and consultants for major building renovations. The institute's call is a proposal to the government, not a decision already taken.

zh.headline: 房屋經理學會促設立法定大廈維修基金
zh.dek: 學會指業主應定期向獨立帳戶供款，以應付2043年前逾2.4萬幢樓齡達50年的維修壓力。
body: 香港房屋經理學會星期四呼籲政府盡早賦予大廈維修基金法定地位，認為業主定期供款，可減輕樓宇老化下突然要籌集大筆維修費的壓力。
學會會長黃汝君表示，業主應設立基金並持續供款，金額一般可按每月管理費的一定比例計算，款項存入獨立、受規管的大廈帳戶，專門用於保養及維修，而不是等到大型工程逼在眉睫才一次過攤分。
她說，希望有關安排可盡早立法。學會引用的估算指，到2043年，本港樓齡達50年或以上的樓宇將超過2.4萬幢。她認為強制性維修基金可把保養由「出事先補」轉為有計劃進行，減輕個別業主負擔，亦可減少對公共財政的壓力。
黃汝君同時歡迎當局為大型樓宇維修設立預先批核的承建商及顧問名單。學會的建議仍是向政府提出的方案，並非已落實的政策。
